source.title: Sparse Feature Circuits: Discovering and Editing Interpretable Causal Graphs in Language Models
source.authors: Samuel Marks; C. Rager; Eric J. Michaud; Yonatan Belinkov; David Bau; Aaron Mueller

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether SAE-derived features in language models can be identified and used as behaviorally relevant units, and examines circuit completeness using causal circuit measurements. It does not reproduce the toy-network geometry experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for SAE-feature and neuron circuits, human interpretability ratings, and feature-ablation classifier experiments. The classifier results below are included because the study removes SAE features and reports the resulting behavior. Other implementation details and cited findings are not study results bearing on these claim versions.
record.test_reason: Most of the paper uses SAE features as a tool for circuit discovery and SHIFT debiasing. Two results bear on the claim versions. First, blind human ratings of Pythia-70M SAE features versus neurons bear on V4. Second, circuit faithfulness and completeness with and without SAE error nodes bear on V4 and V5. The SHIFT classifier results compare the study's own method against baselines and are not tests of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that sparse feature circuits give interpretable causal graphs, and that ablating human-judged spurious SAE features is significantly more effective than a neuron-based ablation (the neuron skyline), which had an unfair advantage. In their limitations they note that components not captured by SAEs stay uninterpretable and that much of the evaluation is qualitative.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE feature dictionaries and causal circuit discovery/editing in language models, rather than testing toy-network superposition geometry or its sparsity-dependent transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ between Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B. Circuit faithfulness varies with circuit size and inclusion of SAE error nodes; classifier outcomes also differ with feature selection and whether the classifier head is retrained.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating human-selected, task-irrelevant SAE features removes a classifier's reliance on gender (gender accuracy near 50%). Random feature ablation has no effect. A neuron skyline fails to match SHIFT and, on Gemma, worsens worst-group accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features permit more targeted causal editing of spurious signals than neurons.

record.problems: The authors state that much evaluation is qualitative, feature labels can vary among annotators and by task, and components not captured by the SAEs remain uninterpretable. The text gives no uncertainty estimates for the reported classifier accuracies or interpretability-rating means; several circuit-curve outcomes are described only qualitatively or shown in figures.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
All of it: capacity competition is not examined.
All of it: no alternative causes of polysemanticity are examined.
Interpretability of Gemma Scope features (the paper defers to Lieberum et al.). How widely features are spread across neurons is not measured.
Stability across seeds or SAE sizes, and canonicality of the features.
All of it: 1-D versus multi-dimensional features are not examined.

missing.what: Numeric faithfulness curves for feature circuits with all SAE errors removed, and with only attention/MLP errors removed, needed to size the V5 incompleteness.

record.verdict_notes: Most rows (r15-r44) are SHIFT method-versus-baseline results and are relinked to none. Interpretability evidence covers Pythia SAEs only and replicates Bricken et al. Raters were ML researchers from ARENA, not a random sample. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-network superposition, feature sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry are not tested.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons result from competition for limited representational capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemantic neurons are evidence of superposition.
Does not measure how broadly features are distributed across neurons in general, or establish that SAE features exhaust the features represented by the models.
Circuit faithfulness/completeness is examined, but feature stability across training runs or settings and canonical status as the model's definitive units are not tested.
Does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features or test whether the model's underlying features are intrinsically one-dimensional.

relation.reason: Although SAEs are also tools for the proposed method, the study independently evaluates feature interpretability, causal relevance, and uncaptured computation.

tranche.reason: Its own human interpretability comparisons and causal circuit evaluations bear on V4 and V5 through methods different from the original toy-model experiments.

source_check.notes: Faithfulness and completeness evaluations exclude the first third of each circuit and use held-out contrastive pairs. Circuit-selected ratings concern the top 30 components by estimated indirect effect; annotator blinding is not stated.

statements.correction: V5 label for this study: limits_scope. Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B subject–verb agreement circuits: residual-stream SAE error removal curtails maximum faithfulness; recovered features retain task-relevant computation but do not capture all of it.
statements.problem: The residual-content finding is accurate, but the challenges label overstates this study's result under the verdict rules: the dictionaries capture computation incompletely.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE-feature circuits and human ratings for Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B
reader_labels.reason: SAE features received higher interpretability ratings than corresponding neuron groups, and feature circuits explained substantial held-out agreement behavior with far fewer nodes than neuron circuits (r4-r10).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Human-selected SHIFT feature ablations and feature skyline on the Bias in Bios task
reader_labels.reason: Feature ablations changed balanced-data classifier behavior, reducing gender accuracy and improving worst-group accuracy; random feature ablations did not, and the feature skyline also produced large changes (r15-r26, r30-r41).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Gemma-2-2B SHIFT without retraining; neuron-skyline comparisons
reader_labels.reason: Gemma's profession accuracy after SHIFT without retraining was limited, while the neuron skyline did not reliably reproduce the feature-edit effects and sometimes moved gender accuracy in the opposite direction (r30, r42-r44).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Subject-verb agreement circuit completeness in Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B
